items.actClause: AN ACT to amend the education law, in relation to enacting the "New York city panel for education policy members public responsibility act"
items.memo:
BILL NUMBER: S2629

SPONSOR: LANZA
 
TITLE OF BILL:  An act to amend the education law, in relation to
enacting the "New York city panel for education policy members public
responsibility act"

 
TITLE OF BILL:

An act to amend the education law, in relation to enacting the "New York
city panel for education policy members public responsibility act"

 
PURPOSE OR GENERAL IDEA OF BILL:

An act that amends the education law requiring a quorum of the Panel
members to attend any public hearing scheduled for the purposes of
allowing for public comment on changes to education plans for public
schools within the New York City school districts.

 
SUMMARY OF SPECIFIC PROVISIONS:

This bill amends the education law by adding a new paragraph (d) to
subdivision 8 of section 2590(g) to require a quorum of the members of
the Panel for Education Policy must attend any hearing scheduled for
purposes of allowing public comments as provided in this section.  In
addition, the Panel may not vote on the proposal unless a quorum of the
members of the Panel attended the hearing relating to such measure. Bill
also defines "attendance", and "Quorum" for purposes of this new legis-
lation.

 
JUSTIFICATION:

The New York City Panel for Education Policy (PEP) is the highest deci-
sion making body for educational policy in the New York City school
district. The PEP, as envisioned and structured by the legislature when
mayoral control was enacted, is an independent body, empowered to make
the final judgment and decisions on education matters including school
specific issues. It is quite clear from legislative history, that it was
the intent of the legislature to have the members of this Panel substan-
tially participate in public hearings required prior to voting and
taking final actions on policy decisions affecting millions of families
in the city district. The current Panel members lack of attendance at
the public hearings on proposals for significant changes in school
utilization plans i.e.  school closure, co-locations, reflects a subter-
fuge approach and a mockery of the democratic process required under
state laws.

The rights of ordinary citizens to appear before the actual members of
the body who will cast the final vote is an indispensable cog of democ-
racy. Under current practice, parents and communities are being forced
to express their concerns and views with regard to proposed changes to
their school at public hearings held by a DOE administrator, not members
of the Panel. This practice under Mayoral-school control has purposeful-
ly circumvented the legislature's intent to provide the public a direct
voice to the final decision makers.

The Panel members who over 98% of time, vote approval of the Chancellor
and DOE's recommendations without the required attendance and partic-
ipation are provided and convenient opportunity to shirk their public
responsibility that comes with the oath of office.  Enactment of this
bill into law will not only clarify the legislature's intent, but also
close the loophole and establish a mechanism that enforces the law and
public responsibility of each Panel member.

 
PRIOR LEGISLATIVE HISTORY:

2016: S.2824 - Passed Senate/A.4811 - Referred to Education
2015: S.2824 - Passed Senate/A.4811 - Referred to Education
2014: S.3615 Referred to Education/A.4811 - Referred to Education
2013: S.3615 Referred to Education/A.4811 - Held in Education
2012: S.7673 - Referred to Rules/A.10409 - Referred to Education

 
FISCAL IMPLICATIONS:

No known fiscal impact.

 
EFFECTIVE DATE:
This act shall take effective immediately.

A.actClause: AN ACT to amend the education law, in relation to enacting the "New York city panel for education policy members public responsibility act"
A.memo:
BILL NUMBER: S2629A          Revised 1/8/18

SPONSOR: LANZA
 
PURPOSE:

An act to amend the education law to require a quorum of the panel
members to attend any public hearing scheduled for the purposes of
allowing public comment on changes to education plans for public schools
within New York City school districts.

 
SUMMARY OF SPECIFIC PROVISIONS:

Section one of the bill provides that the act shall be known as the "New
York City Panel For Education Policy Members Public Responsibility Act"

Section two of the bill adds paragraph (d) to subdivision 8 of § 2590-0
of the education law. Subparagraph (i) requires a quorum of the members
of the panel for education policy (panel) which must attend any hearing
scheduled for purposes of allowing public comment as provided for in
this section. The panel shall not vote on a proposal unless there is a
quorum of the members of the panel.  Subparagraph (ii) defines "attend-
ance" and "quorum" for purposes of this new legislation. Subparagraph
(iii) stipulates that if the panel or chancellor determines that immedi-
ate adoption of an item requiring the approval of the panel is necessary
for the preservation of student health, safety, or general welfare and
that compliance with the quorum requirements would be contrary to the
public interest, then the item may be adopted at a meeting of the panel
on an emergency basis provided that the panel or chancellor provide
written justification for the determination and make it available to the
public on the panel's website. Any item adopted pursuant to this subpar-
agraph will only remain in effect for sixty days. The panel would be
required to meet the requirements of subparagraph (i) of this section
for the item to be adopted on permanently.

Section three of the bill adds subdivision 6 to § 2590-g that is sec to
sunset on June 30, 2017. This section incorporates section two of the
bill into the subdivision.

Section four of the bill provides the effective date.

 
JUSTIFICATION:

The New York City Panel for Education Policy (PEP) is the highest deci-
sion making body for educational policy in the New York City school
district. The PEP, as envisioned and structured by the legislature when
mayoral control was enacted, is an independent body, empowered to make
the final judgment and decisions on education matters including school
specific issues. It is clear that it was the intent of the legislature
to require that the members of this Panel participate in public hearings
prior to voting and taking final actions on policy decisions affecting
millions of families in the New York City school district. Panel
members' lack of attendance at the public hearings regarding proposals
for significant changes in school utilization plans i.e., school
closures and co-locations, reflect a subterfuge approach and a mockery
of the democratic process required under state laws. The rights of ordi-
nary citizens to appear before the actual members of the body who will
cast the final vote is an indispensable cog of democracy. Under current
practice, parents and communities are compelled to express their
concerns and views with regard to proposed changes to their school at
public hearings held by a DOE administrator, not members of the Panel.
This practice under Mayoral school control has purposefully circumvented
the legislature's intent to provide the public with a direct voice to
final decision makers.  The Panel members who primarily vote its
approval of the Chancellor and DOE's recommendations without the
required attendance and participation, are provided with the convenient
opportunity to shirk their public responsibility which comes with the
oath of office.  Enactment of this bill into law will riot only clarify
the legislature's intent, but also close this loophole and establish a
mechanism that enforces the law and public responsibility of each Panel
member.

 
PRIOR LEGISLATIVE HISTORY:

2017:S.2629-A- Passed Senate / A.2949-A- Referred to Education
2016:S.2824-Passed Senate / A.6431- Referred to Education
2015:S.2824-Passed Senate / A.6431- Referred to Education
2014:S.3615-Referred to Education /A.4811 - Referred to Education
2013:S.3615-Referred to Education /A.4811 - Referred to Education
2012:S.7673-Referred to Rules / A.10409 - Referred to Education

 
FISCAL IMPLICATIONS:

No known fiscal impact.

 
EFFECTIVE DATE:
Immediately; provided, however, that the amendments to 5 2590g of the
education law made by section two of this act shall not affect the expi-
ration of such section and shall be deemed to expire therewith.
